books.section: Topic 1.3 European exploration in the Americas
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

primary_sources: Christopher Columbus, letter to Luis de Santangel (1493)

parts.modelAnswer: Columbus claims the peoples he met were gentle and timid, and that they had no iron weapons and gave freely what they had. He presents them as unarmed and welcoming, a claim that shaped how his readers imagined the new lands.
parts.prompt: Identify one claim Columbus makes about the peoples he met.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for naming one accurate claim from the letter, such as the peoples being gentle, timid, unarmed, or generous.
scoring.notEarned: Naming only that Columbus met people, with no claim from the letter, does not earn the point.

parts.modelAnswer: Columbus wrote to report his voyage to the Spanish monarchs and to persuade them that the lands were worth further voyages. His glowing account of fertile land and gold served that purpose, since it promised profit from more expeditions.
parts.prompt: Explain one purpose of Columbus's letter.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining one purpose of the letter, such as reporting the voyage or persuading the monarchs to fund more voyages.
scoring.notEarned: Stating only that Columbus wrote a letter, with no purpose explained, does not earn the point.

parts.modelAnswer: His reports of gold and gentle peoples encouraged Spain to fund more voyages and to claim the lands. The picture he painted of unarmed, welcoming peoples also helped justify conquest, since it suggested the lands could be taken cheaply.
parts.prompt: Explain one way Columbus's account shaped later European action in the Americas.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining one accurate effect of the account, such as further voyages, Spanish claims, or conquest justified by the picture of unarmed peoples.
scoring.notEarned: Stating only that Europeans came to the Americas, with no link to Columbus's account, does not earn the point.

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Christopher Columbus's letter to Luis de Santangel, 1493, public domain.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of Christopher Columbus's letter to Luis de Santangel, written in 1493 after his first voyage. Columbus wrote that the islands he found were fertile and well watered, with great rivers and trees, and that the people were gentle, timid, and well built. He wrote that the people had no weapons of iron and gave freely what they had, and that he believed gold could be found in great quantity. He told the Spanish monarchs that he had taken possession of the lands in their name.
